description: CloudFront distributions must use HTTPS with a secure TLS version for all custom (non-S3) origin connections.

requirements.description: A distribution has no origins defined at all (no custom origins to evaluate).
requirements.rationale: With no custom origins, there is no insecure origin connection to flag. The rule has no applicable target.

requirements.description: A distribution has only S3 (native, non-website) origins and no custom origins.
requirements.rationale: The rule applies only to custom (non-S3) origin connections. Native S3 origins use S3-specific origin configuration and are out of scope.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTP only.
requirements.rationale: An HTTP-only origin protocol policy means CloudFront connects to the origin in plaintext, violating the requirement to use HTTPS for all custom origin connections.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to mirror the viewer's protocol (HTTP when the viewer uses HTTP, HTTPS when the viewer uses HTTPS), regardless of the distribution's viewer protocol policy.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision, match-viewer is flagged unconditionally because origin-level configuration alone must guarantee HTTPS to the origin. Relying on viewer-side enforcement is insufficient.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTPS, and the allowed origin SSL/TLS protocol list contains exclusively secure protocol versions (TLS 1.2 or higher).
requirements.rationale: HTTPS-only with a secure-only TLS protocol list satisfies the rule: every connection to the origin is encrypted with a modern TLS version.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTPS, but the allowed origin SSL/TLS protocol list contains at least one legacy protocol version (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, or TLS 1.1), even if a secure version (TLS 1.2 or higher) is also present.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision (strict mode): the presence of any legacy protocol in the allowed list permits CloudFront to negotiate it with the origin, weakening security.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTPS, but the allowed origin SSL/TLS protocol list contains only legacy protocol versions (e.g., only SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and/or TLS 1.1).
requirements.rationale: All allowed protocols are deprecated/insecure; CloudFront would connect to the origin using a legacy protocol vulnerable to known attacks (e.g., POODLE, BEAST).

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTPS, but the allowed origin SSL/TLS protocol list is omitted entirely.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: the rule requires explicit selection of a secure TLS minimum. An omitted protocol list does not provide an explicit guarantee of a secure floor.

requirements.description: A custom origin is configured to always connect to the origin over HTTPS, but the allowed origin SSL/TLS protocol list is present and empty.
requirements.rationale: An empty allowed-protocol list provides no explicit secure minimum and is not a valid secure configuration.

requirements.description: A custom origin points at an S3 static website hosting endpoint (which only supports HTTP from CloudFront) and uses an HTTP-only origin protocol policy.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: the rule enforces HTTPS for all custom origins regardless of the S3 website endpoint protocol limitation. Users should use a native S3 origin or a different HTTPS-capable fronting mechanism.

requirements.description: A distribution has multiple custom origins where at least one is configured insecurely (HTTP-only, match-viewer, or HTTPS with an insecure/missing TLS protocol list) and others are securely configured.
requirements.rationale: The rule requires HTTPS with a secure TLS version for ALL custom origin connections. Any non-compliant custom origin in the distribution is sufficient to flag.

requirements.description: The custom origin's protocol policy value cannot be determined at analysis time because it depends on an unresolvable input.
requirements.rationale: When the value driving compliance is unknown at analysis time, the rule cannot assert non-compliance and must not produce a false positive.

requirements.description: The custom origin uses HTTPS to the origin, but the contents of the allowed SSL/TLS protocol list cannot be determined at analysis time because they depend on an unresolvable input.
requirements.rationale: Without resolvable protocol values, the rule cannot determine whether any legacy protocol is allowed and must not assert non-compliance.

requirements.description: A distribution has multiple custom origins, all of which are configured for HTTPS-only to the origin with an explicit allowed-protocol list containing only secure TLS versions (TLS 1.2 or higher).
requirements.rationale: Every custom origin meets the requirement of HTTPS with a secure TLS minimum; nothing to flag.
